skill.name: notebooklm
skill.description: Automates Google NotebookLM workflows for notebooks, sources, questions, study materials, and downloadable audio or video artifacts.
skill.summary: Use Google NotebookLM from an AI assistant for research, source analysis, and generated learning artifacts.
skill.author: teng-lin

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by Markdown and JSON strings, not executable Ruby backticks, network clients, or filesystem APIs. However, the package includes audit-bypass style safety claims and instructs agents to perform some NotebookLM account actions without confirmation, which are semantic risks.

remediation.issue: Bundled evaluation content declares the package safe and asserts that findings are false positives.
remediation.suggestion: Remove EVALUATION.json from the published skill package, or move audit artifacts outside the installable skill content.

remediation.issue: The skill allows automatic NotebookLM source imports and notebook actions after activation.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before adding sources, creating notebooks in a user account, or sending any local file or private URL to NotebookLM.

remediation.issue: Authentication guidance references reusable NotebookLM auth state and inline secret material.
remediation.suggestion: Document secret handling requirements, recommended storage controls, and cleanup steps for NOTEBOOKLM_AUTH_JSON and NotebookLM home directories.

content.value_statement: Research workflows often require repetitive NotebookLM setup, source imports, and artifact checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through those tasks using the NotebookLM CLI.
actual_capabilities: Creates, lists, selects, renames, and deletes NotebookLM notebooks through documented CLI commands.
Adds web pages, PDFs, YouTube videos, Google Docs, and text files as NotebookLM sources.
Asks questions against notebook sources and can request answers with citations.
Starts audio, video, quiz, flashcard, mind map, report, and data table generation workflows.
Waits for source processing, research tasks, and generated artifacts when the user requests automation.
Downloads completed audio, video, slide, or image artifacts after confirmation.
limitations: Requires a separate NotebookLM CLI installation and Google authentication before use.
Generation tasks can take several minutes and may fail because of Google rate limits.
The skill depends on NotebookLM behavior and CLI support that may change over time.
Automated source imports can send user-provided material to Google NotebookLM.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Research Notebook
use_cases.description: Create a notebook, add selected sources, and confirm when the material is ready for analysis.

use_cases.title: Create Learning Materials
use_cases.description: Turn class notes or papers into quizzes, flashcards, and study guides for review sessions.

use_cases.title: Produce Source-Based Media
use_cases.description: Generate audio or video overviews from approved sources for internal briefings or content drafts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Notebook
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Use NotebookLM to create a notebook named "{topic}" and show me the notebook ID.

prompt_templates.title: Add and Check Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Add these sources to notebook {notebook_id}: {sources}. Wait until they are ready and summarize their status.

prompt_templates.title: Ask with Citations
prompt_templates.prompt: In notebook {notebook_id}, answer this question using the uploaded sources: {question}. Include source references when available.

prompt_templates.title: Generate and Track Artifact
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an audio overview for notebook {notebook_id} with this focus: {focus}. Track completion and ask before downloading the result.

output_examples.input: Create a NotebookLM notebook for these climate policy papers and prepare a short summary.
output: Notebook created with a clear research title.
Approved sources were added and checked for readiness.
Summary returned with the main themes, disagreements, and source references.

output_examples.input: Turn my lecture notes into quiz material in NotebookLM.
output: A study notebook was prepared from the provided notes.
The quiz generation workflow was started after the sources were ready.
The result status was reported with next steps for review.

output_examples.input: Generate an audio overview from the approved market research sources.
output: The source set was verified before generation.
Audio overview generation was started with the requested focus.
Completion tracking was separated from the main conversation.

best_practices: Authenticate and verify NotebookLM access before starting a multi-step workflow.
Use explicit notebook IDs when more than one agent or account may be active.
Confirm source lists before importing private or sensitive material into NotebookLM.
anti_patterns: Do not import private files or URLs without confirming that the user approves external processing.
Do not rely on shared notebook context during parallel agent workflows.
Do not wait in the main conversation for long artifact generation tasks.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It guides an AI assistant through NotebookLM CLI workflows for notebooks, sources, questions, generated artifacts, and downloads.

faq.question: Does it require a Google account?
faq.answer: Yes. The NotebookLM CLI must be authenticated with a Google account before the workflows can run.

faq.question: Can it upload local files?
faq.answer: Yes, when the user asks to add local files as NotebookLM sources. Confirm sensitive files before import.

faq.question: Can it generate podcasts or videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It can start supported NotebookLM generation workflows and track their completion.

faq.question: Why can generation take a long time?
faq.answer: NotebookLM generation depends on source processing, service load, and Google rate limits.

faq.question: Is this an official Google integration?
faq.answer: No. This is a community skill that documents use of a separate NotebookLM CLI.
